resources.string: Keeps the floating widget active and the microphone ready for push-to-talk.
Tap the widget to chat. Long-press to speak.
Runs while Handy captures the screen to answer a question (API 26–29 fallback).

Handy reads visible on-screen text and the UI tree so the assistant can answer questions about what you see and point at the right button. Handy never taps or types on your behalf in v1. You can turn this off at any time in Settings → Accessibility.
on-screen AI assistant overlay that must remain visible across apps

Handy is an on-screen AI assistant. When you ask a question, Handy reads visible on-screen text via the Android Accessibility service and may capture the active window, then sends your message plus that context to Anthropic (Claude) over HTTPS using your own API key. Optional web-search tools send queries to Brave, Jina, and the public GitHub API only when you enable them in Settings. Handy never taps, types, or scrolls on your behalf. No data is sent to our servers — Handy has none. You can decline any permission and Handy will run in a reduced mode.
Turn on Handy in Accessibility settings
Android will now open Accessibility settings. Find Handy in the list and toggle it on, then press back to return.
Allow Handy to draw over other apps
This is how the floating widget stays visible while you use other apps.
Ask a question, point at a button, or tell Handy to do something like "set a 10-minute timer".
Brave powers general web search, Jina Reader fetches and summarises pages, GitHub searches public repos. Jina + GitHub keys are optional — they raise rate limits.
When on, Claude can call web_search / fetch_page / github_search. Off by default.
Handy can summarize or open your notifications when you ask. Turn this on in Settings to enable.
When the panel or chat is open, Handy can offer to summarize, translate, or rewrite what you just copied. Handy never reads the clipboard in the background.
